newsitem.title: UK: European fuel oil barges start week softer.
newsitem.headline: European fuel oil barges start week softer.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges had a slow start to the week on Monday on the softer side following crude's fall on Friday, with traders saying bunker trade continued thin to mid-day.
Only one trade was reported done at $86 a tonne fob Rotterdam -- or $1.50 less than Friday's highest deal -- before the market was thinly talked with buyers at $85/$86 and sellers at $86/$87 a tonne.
"With Friday's drop in crude prices, it is not surprising that fuel oil was a little weaker," one trader said.
High sulphur barges, pushed up by what traders called regional demand, rose to a level not seen in two months on Friday.
The high sulphur fuel oil cargo market was also quiet early on Monday with players said to be in a wait-and-see mode for the dust to settle from the sharp drop on Friday in NYMEX crude and products.
But some traders said that their assessment called for a stronger market.
"It is a firmer market. There is demand and not too much things on offer and the levels are at about $83, $84, $85 (cif)," one trader said.
